items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: That's when I first met Big Joe Turner. He came there as a singer.

ctx.x: Could you tell me what the house band did at the Dewdrop? I mean, what you all?

We had to play shows. Right. We played some dance numbers, then after that they had shows to come out. We had to play a show. And they had some good shows there. Dancers, singers. That's when I first met Big Joe Turner. He came there as a singer. Then one on the Harris. Then they had Vaughn and Great Truth. They were dancers. They had some nice routines they did. And there was a guy who made a record, a hit record while he was in the service, private, Cecil Gaint. You ever hear of him? Yeah. He came there and we…

Let me back up because I've got something here on you and Ray Charles. It seems you all did a record in 1953 together. You and his band. Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. So was that the first time you got with Ray? Yeah. Okay, because I've got this discography. It says December 4th, 1953. I've forgotten the date.

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: we used to sing down in New Orleans, and we had to go with Jose Hill Band to play behind Joe Turner

ctx.x: What way? For being late. If you, like see, like in the dance, you're supposed to start at nine o'clock. You had to be there for the half. If you come there one second after 8.30, that's a hundred dollar fine. Uh huh. And uh, one day a guy was late, well somebody was always late. One time a guy was late, and he started raising, saying at this guy uh, for being late. And I started laughing, you know. He said, what you laughing at Wallace? He picked me up and said, why don't you laugh at Wallace? I said, I'll tell…

He was a side man. Well how did that, it was fairly common knowledge that he had a drug problem. How did that affect your dealings with him? I don't want to even talk about that. I don't want to talk about that. But it must have had some kind of impact. Or in general dealing with guys in any, in any, in any, in any, in any, in any, in any, in a band in general when they have, when they have drug problems.
